Intensify the statin to high intensity for diabetes with microvascular disease (LDL 108 mg/dL on rosuvastatin 10 mg)
Replace vitamin B12 (raised methylmalonic acid with B12 244 pg/mL on long-term metformin and a polyneuropathy) and monitor B12 while she remains on metformin [BSH_B12_2014]
Manage both gait components: falls prevention and balance physiotherapy, good lighting at home, and foot care for the neuropathy

avoided_actions.rationale: Two years of gradual decline without fluctuation, seizures or rapid progression; EEG would not change the diagnosis.
No tremor, rigidity, fluctuations, hallucinations or dream enactment; a dopamine transporter scan does not address her syndrome.
No Lewy body features; cardiac sympathetic imaging does not address her syndrome and is confounded by diabetic autonomic involvement.
A two-year gradual decline on long-standing diabetes and hypertension is not the subacute multidomain syndrome for which paraneoplastic or autoimmune encephalitis antibodies are indicated.
MRI is available and not contraindicated; CT cannot show microbleeds, siderosis or small lacunes.
No clinical stroke and no cortical or multi-territory infarct; echocardiography has no embolic question to answer in her small-vessel disease.
No clinical stroke and no embolic infarct pattern; prolonged rhythm monitoring would not change management.

key_clinical_evidence: Cognitive testing in a second language systematically overcalls impairment; the fix is first-language and culture-fair instruments, and the deficit here survives that correction
Diabetes drives small-vessel disease directly, and microvascular damage already documented in the retina and the kidney corroborates the same process in the brain

Two gait disorders can coexist: the wide-based low-clearance pattern with dual-task decay is vascular, while visual dependence and a positive Romberg are neuropathic — and each needs its own intervention
Low-normal B12 on long-term metformin, with raised methylmalonic acid, should be corrected on its own merits without being promoted to the explanation of the dementia
Glycaemic targets in an older patient with cognitive impairment must be balanced against hypoglycaemia risk, which itself harms cognition

patient.history_present_illness: Mrs. Harpreet Kaur is a 69-year-old retired seamstress who attends with her daughter-in-law, who interprets. Over two years the family has watched her withdraw from tasks she used to run: she no longer cooks for the household, has twice put salt in the tea, and last winter could not work out how to use the new washing machine although she had used the old one for a decade. Her daughter-in-law is clear that the problem is not language — she has always spoken little Italian — but organisation and speed. She forgets what she was sent to buy but remembers it if reminded of the shop. She is slower in everything and has become quiet. There have been no discrete episodes of weakness, numbness or speech loss. She has fallen twice in the past year, both times in poor light, and her feet have been numb for years. She has had diabetes for twenty-two years with background retinopathy and microalbuminuria and hypertension for twenty. She takes her medication reliably under supervision. There are no hallucinations, no fluctuations, no dream enactment and no tremor. Her thyroid replacement has been stable for eleven years.

neurological_exam.additional: No tremor, no rigidity. No frontal release signs. Two falls in the past year, both in poor light.
neurological_exam.coordination: Intact in the arms; heel-to-shin limited by sensory loss rather than dysmetria.
neurological_exam.cranial_nerves: Pupils equal and reactive. Fundi show background diabetic retinopathy with dot-blot haemorrhages and hard exudates. Extraocular movements full, visual fields full. Face symmetric.
neurological_exam.gait: Short-stepped and wide-based with preserved arm swing; she watches the floor while walking. Romberg positive with eye closure. Tandem impossible.
neurological_exam.mental_status: Alert and cooperative; assessed with an interpreter in Punjabi. Oriented to person and place, gives the year and season correctly. Slow to initiate answers; conversation coherent; naming intact in her first language. Formal cognitive screening reported separately.
neurological_exam.motor: Normal bulk, tone mildly increased in the legs. Strength 5/5 throughout.
neurological_exam.reflexes: 2+ knees, absent ankle jerks bilaterally, plantar responses flexor.
neurological_exam.sensory: Vibration absent at the toes and reduced at the ankles; pinprick reduced in a stocking distribution to mid-calf.
